correctness.rationale: The exact complex-Gaussian integral is valid because Re(2pi-i3lambda tau)=2pi>0. The modulus has no real zeros and Doppler Gaussian integration yields an all-real-parameter moment integral. Tricomi U and p=4 Bessel K0 identities follow from their integral representations. Gaussian-dominated convergence for fixed p<4 and beta-integrability for fixed p>4 yield exact constants; the K0 expansion supplies the critical log. Separate original-integral quadrature and special-function tests passed; numerical checks supplement, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: Self-ambiguity moments are mathematically natural concentration and sharp-inequality invariants. This exact all-order classification displays an integrability-threshold phase change: c^{1-p/2} for p<4, log(c)/c at p=4, and c^{-1} for p>4, with complete constants. It separates global zero-freeness from arbitrarily small higher ambiguity moments, adding natural structural information that general Lieb/Jung inequalities do not supply. No downstream application theorem is asserted.
